holidays.name: National Cherry Turnover Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the flaky, golden pastry stuffed with gooey cherry filling. Bakeries and home cooks alike are encouraged to fold, bake, and devour these handheld treats.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it is an unofficial observance that grew out of food-industry and social media promotion. No single founder is firmly documented.
holidays.funFact: Turnovers are traditionally made by folding dough over the filling into a half-moon or triangle shape, which is where the name 'turnover' comes from.

holidays.name: National Red Wine Day
holidays.description: A day for raising a glass of red wine, from bold Cabernet to silky Pinot Noir. Fans swirl, sniff, and sip while pretending they can detect notes of 'forest floor.'
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance spread by wine lovers and social media. It is one of several wine-themed days on the calendar, and its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: The word 'sommelier' comes from an old French term for a person who handled provisions, and the role evolved into the modern wine expert.

holidays.name: Bow Tie Day
holidays.description: A day for slipping on a bow tie, the neckwear that says 'I'm either very fancy or I'm a game show host.' Wear one to the office, to the grocery store, or while walking the dog.
holidays.origin: An informal fashion observance promoted by bow tie fans and clothiers. It is meant to celebrate a small piece of fabric with a big personality.
holidays.funFact: Bow ties are often traced to Croatian mercenaries in the 17th century, whose neck scarves inspired the French word 'cravate,' the root of 'cravat.'

holidays.name: Rubber Duckie Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the squeaky yellow bath companion that has watched over bubble baths for generations. Duck lovers line up their floating friends and give them a moment of appreciation.
holidays.origin: An informal pop culture observance tied to the beloved bath toy. It also gets a nod from fans of the Sesame Street song 'Rubber Duckie.'
holidays.funFact: In 1992, a shipping container carrying thousands of plastic bath toys fell into the Pacific Ocean, and the toys later helped oceanographers study ocean currents.
